gen_risks.description: Regional conflict in South Sudan may increase refugee inflows, straining water resources and public services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop contingency plans, coordinate with UNHCR and OPM, maintain flexible financing, monitor refugee flows and adjust service delivery as needed.
gen_risks.evidence: continuation of this conflict could affect export earnings and place an excessive amount of pressure on Uganda’s public services and natural resources.

gen_risks.description: Delayed construction and cost overruns due to incomplete designs and inadequate geotechnical studies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct comprehensive feasibility and geotechnical studies before design, include contingency budgets, and adopt robust project management with schedule buffers.
gen_risks.evidence: delayed construction and underestimation of the cost of works; incomplete needs assessments and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies leading to design changes/variations during implementation.

gen_risks.description: Procurement units lack experience with World Bank regulations and are over‑burdened, causing delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit procurement consultants, provide targeted training on World Bank procurement rules, augment PDU staff, and monitor procurement timelines closely.
gen_risks.evidence: PDU staff have no experience in using World Bank Procurement Regulations and Procedures and have a heavy workload; MWE staff have no experience with IDA‑funded procurement.

gen_risks.description: MWE’s Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS) project module is not operational, risking inaccurate financial reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize full implementation of the IFMS project module, establish parallel manual controls, and conduct regular reconciliations and audits.
gen_risks.evidence: The MWE’s IFMS is only operational for government funds, and the project module is not yet fully operational. Project financial reports cannot be generated directly from the IFMS.

gen_risks.description: NWSC may lack capacity to manage the large number of small‑town water schemes transferred under the umbrella model.
gen_risks.mitigation: Phase transfers to NWSC, strengthen NWSC operational capacity, use professionalisation contracts, and provide technical assistance and training.
gen_risks.evidence: NWSC does not have capacity to assume management of all Uganda’s 1,000 + small‑ to medium‑size schemes. The umbrella approach was adopted to address this.

gen_risks.description: Tariffs may be insufficient to achieve full cost recovery, especially in remote or solar‑powered schemes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct cost‑recovery analysis, set progressive tariffs with at least a 25 % margin, include automatic indexation, and monitor revenues for timely adjustments.
gen_risks.evidence: Tariffs must fully cover operating costs and leave a margin of at least 25 %; affordability concerns noted for remote schemes.

gen_risks.description: Climate change (floods, droughts, higher evapotranspiration) could reduce water availability and damage infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑resilient design, implement source‑protection (buffer zones, reforestation), install flood‑control structures, and update water‑availability studies.
gen_risks.evidence: high climate variability and extreme precipitation events likely to cause floods; climate screening identified extreme temperature, increased evapotranspiration, floods.

gen_risks.description: Large labor influx for construction may increase gender‑based violence and social tensions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce a labor influx management plan, require contractor code of conduct, conduct GBV awareness training, and monitor worker camps.
gen_risks.evidence: Labor influx may increase GBV; mitigation includes code of conduct, labor influx management plan, mandatory training on legal conduct and GBV.

gen_risks.description: Construction activities risk environmental contamination (e.g., asbestos cement handling, effluent discharge).
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement ESMPs with strict waste handling, asbestos disposal procedures, effluent treatment standards, and regular environmental monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential adverse environmental impacts include contamination from borehole placement, asbestos cement pipe handling, effluent discharge.

gen_risks.description: Complex coordination among multiple ministries and agencies may cause implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalize coordination protocols, establish clear reporting lines, hold regular inter‑agency meetings, and use the PST to track progress.
gen_risks.evidence: Coordination mechanisms involve multiple departments; WESLD responsible for overall coordination, risk of delays due to complex structure.

gen_risks.description: Report‑based disbursement system may lead to cash‑flow gaps if approvals are delayed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align cash‑flow forecasts with disbursement schedule, maintain buffer funds, and engage donor liaison to expedite approvals.
gen_risks.evidence: Disbursement will be report‑based; withdrawals depend on approved work plans and cash‑flow projections, risk of delayed drawdowns.

gen_risks.description: Non‑compliance with multiple safeguard policies could halt project activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign a dedicated safeguards officer, conduct regular compliance audits, train staff on OP/BP policies, and maintain up‑to‑date documentation.
gen_risks.evidence: Project triggers safeguards policies on Environmental Assessment, Involuntary Resettlement, Safety of Dams, International Waterways, Forests, Natural Habitats, Physical Cultural Resources.

gen_risks.description: High non‑revenue water (NRW) in new schemes may erode financial viability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Install metering, conduct leak detection, implement NRW reduction program, and train operators on water loss management.
gen_risks.evidence: NRW at 29 % in small towns; high NRW can affect financial viability.

gen_risks.description: Excessive groundwater extraction could deplete aquifers and compromise sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Carry out comprehensive groundwater assessments, set extraction limits, monitor water tables, and develop a groundwater management toolkit.
gen_risks.evidence: Groundwater sustainability concerns; excessive groundwater development localized; need for groundwater assessment and monitoring.

gen_risks.description: Limited capacity of domestic contractors may force reliance on international firms, raising costs and schedule risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct market sounding, encourage joint ventures, provide capacity‑building for local firms, and allow selective international participation where needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Limited domestic contracting capacity to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope; most contracts will be done by international firms.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk: as detailed in the CPF, significant political uncertainty is not foreseen, but governance and effective public-sector management present substantial risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will mitigate these risks through (a) strengthening the MWE's regulatory framework; (b) carrying out a citizen engagement strategy; and (c) strengthening project implementation efforts in close coordination with local government officials and development partners. The World Bank's procurement processes will also help safeguard the Project from corruption.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk: the Umbrella Water Authority (UWA) as a regional service delivery model for small towns and RGCs was recently introduced. Although the decision to scale up this model was informed by extensive analytical work and a pilot project, the UWA model was only recently operationalized.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will support implementation of a professionalized monitoring system focused on enhancing revenue collection approaches (billing software, cashless/mobile payment systems) and on strengthening integration of specialized private operators through improved contract management. The implementation team will use the Utility Performance Monitoring and Information System (UPMIS) tool to regularly review UWA and NWSC performance.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk: the Procurement risk is rated Substantial while the FM risk is Moderate. The risks identified relate to delays and skills gaps at different stages of procurement processing.
gt_risks.mitigation: IWMDP will benefit from the lessons learned and mechanisms put in place under the predecessor project (WMDP); detailed mitigation measures for the procurement risk are set out in the Appraisal (Procurement) section.

gt_risks.description: The environmental and social risk is deemed Substantial given (a) potential opposition to the introduction of a new service delivery model, including new tariffs and catchment management measures; (b) the influx of new workers in small towns and RGCs; and (c) potentially adverse environmental impacts from the construction and operation of the proposed investments.
gt_risks.mitigation: The environmental and social risk will be managed through the application of an Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and related safeguards instruments (Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, Resettlement Action Plans).

gt_risks.description: Other risks (social tensions in districts hosting refugees): tensions between refugees and citizens are caused by inequity in access to and payment for water supply and sanitation (WSS) services. While refugees in the settlements benefit from humanitarian aid and GoU support, Ugandans in host communities receive limited support for services and infrastructure, causing social tension that may result in Project implementation delays given potential community opposition to the works.
gt_risks.mitigation: The GoU has prioritized development efforts for poor districts hosting refugees while remaining firmly committed to its policy on refugee protection. The Project will manage this risk by designing WSS facilities and catchment management measures that benefit both host communities and refugees, and by ensuring the Project's social and communication management plan is applied and adequately supervised. There are no known existing risks to the refugee protection framework or reputational risks for the Project.
